Wenn ich ein neues Notizdokument öffne, kann ich nicht mehr wie gewohnt direkt mit meiner Tastatur schreiben. In Quicknotes funktioniert die Tastatur komischerweise weiterhin problemlos. Auch in älteren Dokumenten kann ich sie noch ganz normal verwenden, sofern ich dort bereits zuvor mit der Tastatur geschrieben habe.

Vor dem Update konnte ich einfach auf „Mit Tippen starten“ drücken und direkt im Dokument losschreiben. Der Text wurde dabei automatisch an die vorhandenen Linien oder Kästchen angepasst und genau dort eingefügt, wo er hingehört.

Jetzt funktioniert das plötzlich nicht mehr. Stattdessen muss ich umständlich ein Textfeld erstellen, das dann auch noch irgendwo im Dokument platziert wird. Dieses lässt sich nicht wie zuvor direkt in die vorgegebenen Linien oder Kästchen integrieren. Damit geht genau die Funktion verloren, die das Schreiben mit der Tastatur in Goodnotes so praktisch gemacht hat.

Ich verstehe wirklich nicht, warum eine zuvor einwandfrei funktionierende und grundlegende Funktion durch ein Update verschlechtert wird. Es kann doch nicht sein, dass man sich plötzlich mit umständlichen Textfeldern herumschlagen muss, obwohl es vorher eine einfache und funktionierende Lösung gab.

reviews.title: I Miss GoodNotes 5 And After the Latest Update, I Can’t Even Go Back to It Despite Having Paid for
reviews.text:
GoodNotes used to be a simple, reliable, and genuinely excellent note-taking app. GoodNotes 5, in particular, did exactly what it was supposed to do: it let me write, organize, edit, and study without constantly fighting the app itself.

Now, after the recent updates, that reliability feels almost gone.

I am dealing with bugs that should never exist in an app built around something as basic as note-taking. I delete text, leave the document, reopen it, and somehow the deleted text is back again. At that point, I am no longer editing my notes — I am negotiating with them.

The interface has also become increasingly frustrating. Features and tools that used to be straightforward now feel unnecessarily complicated, buried, changed, or redesigned for no convincing reason. Instead of improving the workflow, many updates seem to interfere with a workflow that already worked perfectly well.

And this is the part that frustrates me most: I actually paid for GoodNotes 5, and I preferred it. Yet after the latest changes, I cannot simply return to the version of the product I originally paid for and trusted.

Why should longtime users lose access to the experience they purchased just because the company decided to keep redesigning the app?

Not every product needs to become more complex. Not every update is an improvement. Adding more features means very little when basic functions become unreliable.

reviews.title: App needs work.  Not intuitive at all
reviews.text: I give credit to the Goodnotes people because they reached out to me in response to my previous critical review.  Unfortunately, the answer was to read voluminous articles and instruction manuals.  This is not going to happen.  I need the app to be intuitive so that a genius like me can use the app without reading tons of material.  I have great expertise running all sorts of apps and I agree that some apps should be subject to expertise that is gained through reading manuals.  For crying out loud, this is a NOTES app!  It should be simple.  I was told that I could use it to record all of the information that I need about photographs I take with vintage film cameras.  Digital cameras do this all automatically, but I shoot film which means that I need a simple app to record all the data for each shot I take like: Film type, format, shutter speed, aperture, exposure index, atmospheric conditions, zone system offsets, developer push/pull recommendation, etc.  This app is not it.  It is hard enough for me to figure out all the camera settings I need to take the perfect shot.  It is critical that I be able to document all of the factors that make up the perfect shot so that I can apply the same principles to future images.  To do this, I need a good Notes App that is easy to use that I do not need to divert my intellect away from applying it to my photography.  This app ain’t it.

reviews.title: Appalling Ease of Use for a 75-Year-Old Lifetime “Special Edition” User
reviews.text:
I am a paying lifetime “Special Edition” user who purchased Goodnotes through the Apple App Store on 6 September 2023.

I appreciate the power and design of the application, but I must honestly express disappointment regarding accessibility and usability for older users and people with cognitive or visual difficulties.

I am using the latest iPad Pro 13” M5 (2025), so the issues I describe are not related to outdated hardware.

Despite paying for the premium lifetime “Special Edition” version through the App Store, basic accessibility and reading features still appear to be missing, including:

• Infinite scrolling text
• Automatic text reflow when increasing font sizes
• Zoom lock or protection against accidental zooming
• Easier adaptive page rendering
• Simpler document handling for elderly and disabled users

At 75 years old, with eyesight difficulties and ADHD, I find it extremely frustrating that enlarging text for readability often breaks the layout of the page and forces constant manual adjustment of zoom and formatting.

Modern note-taking applications should adapt to the user — especially paying users — rather than requiring constant technical management of page rendering and scaling.

reviews.title: Great app but one main issue about battery and overheating
reviews.text: Over the past 6 months I’ve been using Goodnotes extensively, for more than 8 hours a day at certain points. There’s lots I’ve loved, from the different options of pens and papers to use as well as how simple it is to upload files to write and annotate over. However, this week I’ve had to switch over to Noteful and the reason behind this is entirely due to what I believe is optimisation issues within the app. While writing on my Ipad, my screen starts heating up almost instantly to the point where it starts becoming painful to touch. It also has been eating away at my battery health, where an IPad I brought at the beginning of the year has dropped in battery health to 88% despite being brand new less than 6 months ago. This is a massive issue as a few days ago it began heating up so much to the point where my IPad stopped charging completely, even after I had closed the app. I am unsure why a note taking app does require so much battery but due to this I have had to switch to alternatives as it continues to degrade my Ipad and I worry that one day it will just crash and I will lose all work I have been going through. Should Goodnotes fix these overheating and battery issues I’d love to come back as other note taking apps can’t compete but sadly for the time being the issue is to large to tolerate any longer :(

reviews.title: Misleading Plans, Refund Obstacles, and Wasted Money. Do not waste your time
reviews.text:
I subscribed to the Essential plan on March 5th ($11.99) because the membership information clearly suggested cross-compatibility across devices. That was the entire reason I purchased it.
Shortly after subscribing, I was told that this was misleading and that Essential would not provide full cross-platform functionality, and that I needed to upgrade to Pro. So on March 10th, just five days later, I upgraded to Pro and was charged $35.99 in full again.
I paid twice within five days based on unclear and misleading subscription descriptions.
Even after upgrading, cross-compatibility still does not properly work on Windows because the Windows version restricts OneDrive sign-in to personal Microsoft accounts only. The exact same university Microsoft account works perfectly on iPad but is blocked on Windows, something that was never made clear before subscribing.
When I tried to refund via Paddle, the receipts were tied to an Apple relay email generated during checkout. The verification emails would not forward properly, making it impossible to retrieve receipts. I provided card details for manual lookup and still had to chase support for basic billing resolution. There is no proper live support, and responses are slow.
I am a medical student. I rely on reliable cross-platform access for my coursework, and I do not have time to spend hours troubleshooting subscription tiers, cloud restrictions, and billing verification loops that should not exist in the first place.

reviews.title: 2 years of using
reviews.text:
Unfortunately, the app’s performance has been declining month by month. I used it during the first semester without any issues. However, in the second and third semesters, I began experiencing several problems, including poor drawing quality, device overheating, frequent pen snapping and cut-offs, rapid battery consumption, and a noticeable decrease in battery life.
One of the main issues I faced was related to Apple’s warranty. I initially believed the problem was with my Apple Pencil, so I sent it in multiple times. Each time, I was told there was no issue. Eventually, one of Apple’s support representatives suggested testing the pen on another app, such as Apple Notes. They were absolutely right the pen worked smoothly and wrote clearly there.

As time went on, there were so many add-ons and different features added to the app and its basic functions started to worsen. I would need to refresh the app multiple times on my iPad, oftentimes mid-lecture, to be able to write effectively. And the texting feature is terrible, it barely works on my laptop and it no longer covers my basic needs. Im really disappointed because I used to love this app.

reviews.title: Goodnotes 6 schrecklich
reviews.text:
Ich hab mir vor Ewigkeit in meiner Schulzeit Goodnotes geholt und war sehr begeistert ich hab es immer auf meinem IPad genutzt, konnte damit Zeichen aber auch die Schreibfunktion mit der Tastatur nutzen. Seit ich auf Goodnotes 6 umsteigen musste funktioniert gar nichts mehr. Das System stürzt die ganze Zeit App ohne meine Sachen zu speichern also konnte ich jetzt schon mehrmals meine Arbeit wiederholen und die Tools sind auf völlig schrecklich, man kennt sich überhaupt nicht aus und es ist unglaublich umständlich alles zu verwenden. Dabei bin ich Mitte 20 und habe sonst keine Probleme mit jeglichen Apps. 
Unglaublich traurig wie sich das entwickelt konnte vor 3-4 Jahren habe ich jeden diese App empfohlen. 
Bitte einfach Goodnotes 6 mit dem selben Layout und Benutzerhandbuch von Goodnotes 5 umstellen!

reviews.text: I loved this app before the update. I bought it a couple months ago and paid for it. I was using the free version before and loved it so I decided to buy the lifetime version. About a week later it got this absolutely HORRENDOUS update it’s really infuriating. There was no need for a floating tool bar as the tools being at the top was much more convenient and out the way and iPads have a tool bar at the bottom of the screen. It’s so frustrating as the floating tool bar covers text, whole sentences and when I’m trying to change text I can’t change it because it’s either being covered by the tool bar or it’s disappeared because the text is too high or low on the page. The lasso tool is a default and is the bane of my existence. It’s so inconvenient and It is a great tool just not as a default tool. The grammar also needs work everything is a default lower case. This needs change. Wouldn’t recommend this app to anyone anymore.
